hints.title: Cost of Matching Characters
hints.text: Making strings equal by character deletions is equivalent to finding a common subsequence that maximizes the sum of preserved characters.

hints.title: State Definition
hints.text: Let dp[i][j] represent the minimum deletion cost to equalize prefixes s1[0...i] and s2[0...j].

hints.title: Transition Conditions
hints.text: If characters s1[i-1] and s2[j-1] match, the cost equals dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise take the minimum of deleting s1[i-1] costing ord(s1[i-1]) + dp[i-1][j] and deleting s2[j-1] costing ord(s2[j-1]) + dp[i][j-1].

complexity.notes: 2D dynamic programming grid computing minimum weighted deletion edits.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursively testing all deletion subsets explores an exponential O(2^(M+N)) states.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tabulating subproblems avoids redundant calculations, optimizable to O(N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Model base cases with cumulative ASCII sums and transition on matching characters.
